e3aad61a-89b4-46a6-8c16-6f80b861d717.name: Welcome to the Luxembourg Museum! I’m your digital museum guide.

18c02a46-9083-4b99-a0d8-ce19b0daa883.name: You are standing in front of the Fortress Model, a scale representation of the historic fortifications of Luxembourg City.

e8a9cdc6-58cc-4f70-9719-a283152e97fc.name: For centuries, Luxembourg was one of Europe’s most heavily fortified cities. Its walls, bastions, gates, and steep surrounding valleys made it an important military stronghold.

26f5870d-1c05-4058-8303-09ddf08e9697.name: Look closely at the model and you can see how the old city was protected by several layers of defensive structures. Many of these fortifications were dismantled in the nineteenth century, but traces of them can still be seen across Luxembourg City today.

aeec99e7-7625-4964-a036-c73f8d0d867b.name: You are standing in front of the Historic Tram, an exhibit showing the development of public transport in Luxembourg City.

7271a943-da88-4fac-9fe8-9a053948a05e.name: Trams once played an important role in connecting the city centre with surrounding neighbourhoods. Over time, buses and cars became more common, and the original tram network disappeared.  Decades later, trams returned to Luxembourg as part of a modern public transport system. This exhibit shows how urban transport has changed over time and how the tram has become part of the city again.

266d70f0-d20b-47ef-9451-14f6b57946ec.name: The museum is open from 10:00 to 18:00.

db921cf5-ce72-4201-9131-bf781ce2700a.name: A standard ticket costs €10. Reduced admission is €6.

02b80ce4-e4fa-42c1-803d-f01d5a520b77.name:
Enter the museum using the main stairs and entrance. An elevator is also available for accessible entry.

Once inside, you will find the Fortress Model on your left and the Historic Tram on your right.

To leave the museum, continue straight ahead toward the exit stairs. An accessibility platform is available there as well.

components.content: Explore Luxembourg City's past through a model of its historic fortress and an exhibit about the city's tram network. Plan your visit and discover what to see.
See a scale model of Luxembourg City's historic walls, gates and bastions. Many of the fortifications were dismantled in the nineteenth century.
Learn how trams once connected the city centre with nearby neighbourhoods, disappeared as transport changed, and later returned to Luxembourg City.
Use the main entrance stairs or the accessible lift. In the exhibition room, the Fortress Model is
. The exit is straight ahead, with stairs or an accessibility platform.
